title: Experimental observation of the prior residence advantage in masu salmon in an experimental channel
content:
Experimental stocking trials were conducted in an artificial channel with multiple pools to evaluated the extent of prior resident advantage on post-stocking competition for favourable territory in masu salmon, which is widely stocked in Japanese streams. Stocked intruder fish were more likely to move out of the artificial channel by migrating downstream compared to prior resident fish. Stocking of masu salmon may be ineffective in streams with prior resident fish and few available habitats as most stocked fish are unable to settle at the site stocked.


Abstract

Stocking of hatchery-reared salmonids is still a common management strategy to supplement natural resources and improve recreational fishing catch. However, concerns have been raised about the effectiveness of stocking as there is evidence that stocked fish may replace prior resident fish or fail to settle at the intended stocking sites, resulting in downstream emigration and may subsequently die. This study evaluated whether stocked masu salmon (Oncorhynchus masou masou), a species widely stocked in Japanese streams, displace prior resident fish or emigrate from stocked site. Experimental stocking trials were conducted in an artificial channel with multiple pools where factors potentially affecting the interactions between residents and intruders can be controlled. We found that stocked intruder fish were more likely to move out of the artificial channel compared to prior resident fish. Our findings indicate that stocking of masu salmon may be ineffective in streams with prior resident fish and few available habitats as most stocked fish are unable to settle at the site stocked. Practical implication: To optimize stocking efficiency for species, which show prior residence advantage such as masu salmon, stocking should only occur in situations where suitable, unoccupied habitats are available and where site fidelity of stocked fish can be expected.

要旨

人工孵化由来のサケ科魚類の放流は現在でも天然資源を補填し，遊漁の漁獲量を向上させるための一般的な管理手法となっている.しかし，放流先の河川において，後から侵入した放流魚が先住魚を置換したり，増殖予定域に定着できずに下流に流出し，その後死亡する可能性があるという知見が集積されつつあることにより，放流の効果についての懸念が生じている. 本研究では，日本の河川で広く放流されているサケ科魚類であるヤマメを放流した場合，先住魚を置換するのか，あるいは放流場所から流下移動するのかを評価した.実験は，定住魚と侵入魚の相互作用に影響を及ぼす可能性のある他の要因を制御した，複数のプールを有する人工水路で実施した. 放流した侵入魚は先住魚に比べて人工水路の外へ移動する確率が高かった.この結果は，放流魚の多くは放流地点に定着することができないことから，先住魚が占有していることで利用可能な生息場所が少ない河川では，ヤマメの放流は効果がない可能性を示唆している. ヤマメのような先住効果を示す種の放流効果を最適化するためには，未占有の適切な生息場所が存在し，放流魚の定着が期待できる状況でのみ放流を行うべきである.
